title: Relabel a hard word, keep the idea
statement: Judge a technical term by whether learners can build its concept now, and where only the word is too hard, give it a plain label and keep the idea.
detail: The grade-7 science script rules replace a banned-word list with one question asked of every term the central idea touches, whether a learner of the grade can build the concept right now, and scripts are drafted from the result (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7-science/brainlifts/script-generation-v0.1.md`, lines 68 and 88). A term in reach, or load-bearing and teachable in plain words, is kept; one whose idea belongs but whose word is too technical is simplified by leading with a plain label and naming the precise term once; and a term is dropped only when it is both above grade and unnecessary to the central idea. Coverage wins over vocabulary: a load-bearing idea is never dropped because its usual word is hard.

evidence.quote: SIMPLIFY if the idea belongs but the word is too technical (lead with a plain label, name the precise term once); DROP only if above grade AND unnecessary to land the hinge. Coverage wins over vocabulary — never drop a load-bearing idea because its usual word is hard; relabel and keep the idea.
run KEEP/SIMPLIFY/DROP over every term the hinge touches; draft from the *result*, not the raw topic.
